mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a quarter indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE was below 4% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer and business confidence rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both HOUST and GDPC1 increased over a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 3% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three consecutive months signal a weakening supply side and labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity contracts.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decline and UNRATE increase over 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO declined and UNRATE increased over three consecutive months.
